column1: # What `image` 0.25.10 does with every file of the BMP conformance suite, through this
# Committed so a dependency bump that moves one file's behaviour is visible rather than
# absorbed. `tests/image_pages.rs` reads this and fails naming any row that moved.
# The suite's directories are its author's judgement about BMP, not about this tool:
#   g/  a BMP reader must read these        27 read, 0 refused
#   q/  unusual, obsolete, arguably invalid 31 read, 10 refused
#   b/  clearly invalid; must not crash     5 read, 15 refused
# Four of the five `b/` files that read are accepted because their invalidity is in metadata
# the decoder does not consult: each decodes at the correct 127x64 geometry, which
# `b/pal8badindex.bmp` is the exception, measured rather than assumed. Its invalidity is in
# the pixel data, and `image` zero-fills its palette to 256 entries, so 4,793 of its 8,128
# pixels — 59% of the page — decode as black. It is accepted on cost, not on the argument
# above: detecting it needs the declared palette size and a pass over the index plane, which
# `image`'s API cannot supply and which amounts to a second BMP reader. No real comic archive
# holds such a file. The behaviour is pinned exactly by
# `an_out_of_range_palette_index_decodes_as_black`, so a change upstream reopens the
